Jacinth
JAY-sinth
noun
Greek huakinthos (G5191/G5192) — a precious stone of deep blue or blue-violet color, identified today as a variety of zircon or sapphire; the eleventh foundation of the New Jerusalem (Rev 21:20). The same Greek word names the flower hyacinth.

📖 Biblical Definition

Jacinth is the eleventh foundation stone of the New Jerusalem (Rev 21:20). The Greek huakinthos covers both a flower (hyacinth) and a deep blue-violet stone, probably modern zircon or sapphire. The same word appears in Revelation 9:17 describing the breastplates of the demonic horsemen of the sixth trumpet: "having breastplates of fire, and of jacinth, and brimstone" — fire (red), jacinth (deep blue), brimstone (sulfur-yellow) — the colors of judgment. Yet here in Revelation 21 the same color crowns the eleventh course of the city's eternal foundation. Eleven is sometimes the biblical number of incompleteness or transition (eleven faithful disciples after Judas fell, before Matthias was chosen, Acts 1:26; eleven days from Horeb to Kadesh-Barnea, Deut 1:2 — the journey Israel could have completed in eleven days but turned into forty years through unbelief). The eleventh foundation, jacinth, sits at the threshold of the city's completion — one stone shy of the twelfth and final stone. The blue-violet of jacinth pictures the deep of heaven; the city's penultimate foundation reaches into that blue. In the high priestly garments the blue of the ephod and the blue of the lace fastening the breastplate to the ephod (Exod 28:28, 31, 37) recurs throughout — blue is the priestly color of heavenly origin. Jacinth gathers up that thread into the foundation of the city where every priest-believer reigns with Christ.

A deep blue-violet precious stone; the eleventh foundation of the New Jerusalem.

JACINTH, noun. A precious stone of a deep blue or blue-violet color, identified today as a variety of zircon (the orange-yellow variety) or sometimes as sapphire (the blue variety). Anciently associated with the hyacinth flower's deep color.

In Scripture, the eleventh foundation of the New Jerusalem (Rev 21:20); the color of the demonic horsemen's breastplates in the sixth trumpet vision (Rev 9:17); related by name to the hyacinth flower.

📖 Key Scripture

Revelation 21:20 — "The tenth, a chrysoprasus; the eleventh, a jacinth; the twelfth, an amethyst."

Revelation 9:17 — "And thus I saw the horses in the vision, and them that sat on them, having breastplates of fire, and of jacinth, and brimstone."

Exodus 28:28 — "And they shall bind the breastplate by the rings thereof unto the rings of the ephod with a lace of blue, that it may be above the curious girdle of the ephod."

Numbers 15:38 — "Speak unto the children of Israel, and bid them that they make them fringes in the borders of their garments throughout their generations, and that they put upon the fringe of the borders a ribband of blue."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

Jacinth is corrupted when the canonical bookending — same word in Rev 9:17 (demonic horsemen) and Rev 21:20 (city foundation) — is missed, blunting the biblical reversal of colors of judgment becoming colors of glory.

expand to see more

Color-as-coincidence reading. The Greek huakinthos appears in Revelation in two opposite contexts: the breastplates of judgment-horsemen (9:17) and the foundation of the eternal city (21:20). Modernist commentary often treats this as coincidence — the same color is used because it's a natural color for stones AND for breastplates. But Revelation is a deeply patterned book; the SAME word in opposite contexts is the Spirit's deliberate juxtaposition. Judgment colors and city colors meet at jacinth — and the color of fearful trumpet-judgments becomes the color of the eternal city's penultimate foundation.

Blue-thread severance. The OT priestly garments use BLUE pervasively — the lace fastening the breastplate (Exod 28:28), the robe (28:31), the cord on the high priest's mitre (28:37), the borders of every Israelite's garment (Num 15:38). Blue is the priestly color, the color of heavenly origin in the OT typology. To strip the OT blue thread from the eleventh foundation of the city is to lose the priestly-eschatological connection: the blue we once wore around our garments now FOUNDS the city in which we reign as kings and priests (Rev 5:10).

Greek huakinthos (G5191/G5192) — jacinth; both a flower (hyacinth) and a precious stone of deep blue-violet color

Eleventh foundation stone of New Jerusalem (Rev 21:20); appears also at Rev 9:17 as a breastplate color of judgment horsemen

Usage

"The eleventh foundation is jacinth — the blue that once threaded the priest's garments now founds the city of priest-kings."

"The same color that armored the demonic horsemen of trumpet six now beds the city of God: the colors of judgment are reclaimed into the colors of glory."

"Blue in Scripture is heavenly; jacinth lays heaven into the eternal city's eleventh course."
